author: krishagel
body:
## Summary
Implements comprehensive TypeScript type safety for Server-Sent Events (SSE) to prevent field name mismatches and improve developer experience across all streaming implementations.

## Problem
The recent bug (#367) revealed that SSE event handlers lacked type safety, causing runtime field name mismatches (e.g., `textDelta` vs `delta`) that led to silent failures where streaming content was not displayed to users.

## Solution

### 1. New Type System (`/lib/streaming/sse-event-types.ts`)
Created comprehensive TypeScript type definitions including:
- **20+ event type interfaces** covering all Vercel AI SDK v5 SSE events
- **Discriminated union type** (`SSEEvent`) for exhaustive type checking
- **Type guards** for runtime validation of each event type
- **Parsing functions** with error handling and recovery
- **Extensive JSDoc documentation** for all types

### 2. Event Types Covered
- **Text Streaming**: `text-start`, `text-delta`, `text-end`
- **Reasoning (O1/O3)**: `reasoning-start`, `reasoning-delta`, `reasoning-end`
- **Tool Execution**: `tool-call`, `tool-call-delta`, `tool-input-start`, `tool-input-error`, `tool-output-error`, `tool-output-available`
- **Lifecycle**: `start`, `start-step`, `finish-step`, `finish`
- **Messages**: `message`, `assistant-message`
- **Errors**: `error`

### 3. Component Updates
Updated Assistant Architect streaming component:
- Replaced manual `JSON.parse()` with typed `parseSSEEvent()`
- Replaced string-based type checking with type guards
- All event handlers now have compile-time type safety
- TypeScript compiler will catch field name errors before runtime

## Benefits
✅ **Compile-time errors** if wrong field names are used  
✅ **IDE autocomplete** shows correct field names  
✅ **Type guards** provide runtime safety  
✅ **Single source of truth** for SSE event structures  
✅ **Easy to update** when Vercel AI SDK changes  
✅ **Prevents bugs** like the recent `delta`/`textDelta` mismatch

## Code Example

**Before (unsafe):**
```typescript
const parsed = JSON.parse(data);
if (parsed.type === 'text-delta' && parsed.textDelta) {
  // BUG: Field is 'delta', not 'textDelta' - silent failure!
  text += parsed.textDelta;
}
```

**After (type-safe):**
```typescript
const event = parseSSEEvent(data);
if (isTextDeltaEvent(event)) {
  // TypeScript error if you use 'textDelta'!
  text += event.delta; // ✅ Correct field
}
```

## Testing
- ✅ TypeScript compilation passes (`npm run typecheck`)
- ✅ ESLint validation passes (`npm run lint`)
- ✅ No breaking changes to existing functionality
- ✅ Type guards add minimal overhead (<1ms per event)

## Files Changed
- **New**: `/lib/streaming/sse-event-types.ts` (530 lines)
- **Modified**: `/components/features/assistant-architect/assistant-architect-streaming.tsx`

## Migration Notes
- Types are additive - existing code continues to work
- Type guards validate structure at runtime
- Legacy event formats still supported for backward compatibility
- Future work: Apply types to Nexus Chat streaming handlers (tracked separately)

## Related Issues & PRs
- Closes #363
- Related to PR #367 (fix for delta/textDelta field mismatch)

## Deployment Notes
- No database migrations required
- No environment variable changes
- No infrastructure changes
- Safe to deploy immediately
- Zero runtime performance impact

## Checklist
- [x] Code follows project style guidelines
- [x] TypeScript compilation passes
- [x] ESLint passes
- [x] No breaking changes
- [x] Issue will auto-close when PR merges
- [x] Commit messages are detailed and descriptive

## Next Steps
This implementation covers the Assistant Architect streaming component. Future PRs can:
1. Apply types to Nexus Chat streaming handlers
2. Apply types to unified streaming service
3. Add unit tests for type guards and parsers
4. Add runtime monitoring for unrecognized event types

body:
## 🎯 Project 5 – Guess the Number Game

### 🚀 Features Implemented

#### 🏁 Start Screen
- Displays the app interface with initial instructions
- Shows input field and "Guess" button
- Initializes attempt counter to 10 and error counter to 0
- Input field is empty on load

#### 🎮 Game Flow
- User enters a number and presses "Guess"
- App logs the guessed number to the console
- Displays feedback based on guess (too high, too low, correct)
- Updates remaining attempts and error count
- Shows how many attempts were used if guessed correctly
- Reveals correct number if attempts run out

#### 🔄 Game End & Restart
- Displays result message (win or lose)
- Resets input field and counters
- Allows user to start a new game
- Ensures counters do not reset prematurely

#### 😢 Sad Path Handling
- Decreases attempt count on incorrect guesses
- Displays message when no attempts remain
- Reveals correct number
- Resets input field and disables guess button

### 📦 Changes Made

- 🧩 Created `GuessTheNumberComponent` with encapsulated game logic
- 🎨 Applied layout and styling for game flow and feedback
- 🖼️ Added game preview image to `public/images/guess-the-number.png`
- 🔗 Registered project in `PROJECT_COMPONENTS_MAP` as day 5
- 🧠 Implemented input validation, feedback messaging, and game state transitions

### 🔍 Preview

The app provides an interactive number guessing experience with clear feedback, attempt tracking, and win/loss conditions. Fully integrated into the SPA and accessible via the project navigation.

### 🔜 Next Steps

- 🌐 Add localization support for messages (English/Spanish)
- 📊 Display guess history visually
- ✨ Add animations for feedback transitions

author: simon-duchastel
body:
## Summary
- Implements long-term memory (LTM) system following the same pattern as short-term memory (STM)
- LTM retrieval uses LLM-based file selection via dynamically generated mind map
- LTM update promotes important STM memories when token threshold is exceeded
- Creates repository abstraction for LTM file operations

## Implementation Details

### LongTermMemoryRepository
- Manages LTM files in `~/.brainiac/long-term-memory/` directory
- `listFiles()` - Recursively lists all LTM file paths
- `read(relativePath)` - Reads specific LTM file content
- `write(relativePath, content)` - Writes content to LTM file
- `generateMindMap()` - Creates XML representation of directory tree (file/folder names only, no content)

### recallLongTermMemory()
1. Generates XML mind map of LTM directory structure
2. Asks LLM to identify which files would be helpful given the user request and mind map
3. Reads all identified files
4. Returns concatenated memory content

### updateLongTermMemory()
1. Checks if STM exceeds 10,000 token threshold
2. When exceeded:
   - Asks LLM to identify important memories from STM to promote
   - Writes promoted memories to LTM files (LLM provides filenames)
   - Asks LLM to clean/condense STM by removing promoted/unneeded info
   - Updates STM repository with cleaned version

## Changes
- Created `LongTermMemoryRepository.kt` with file operations and mind map generation
- Implemented `recallLongTermMemory()` in `LongTermMemory.kt`
- Implemented `updateLongTermMemory()` in `LongTermMemory.kt`
- Updated `CoreLoop` to accept and use `LongTermMemoryRepository`
- Updated `CoreAgent` to accept and pass `LongTermMemoryRepository`
- Updated CLI `Main.kt` to instantiate `LongTermMemoryRepository`

## Test Plan
- [ ] Verify build passes
- [ ] Test LTM retrieval with existing files
- [ ] Test LTM promotion when STM exceeds threshold
- [ ] Verify mind map generation for nested directories
- [ ] Test STM cleaning after promotion

author: copilot
body:
## Summary

This PR backports the security patch for **CVE-2025-27515** (GHSA-78fx-h6xr-vch4) from Laravel 12 to Laravel 9, addressing a critical file validation bypass vulnerability that could allow attackers to circumvent File and Password validation rules using specially crafted array keys.

## Vulnerability Description

The vulnerability allowed attackers to bypass validation by submitting data with array keys that match internal placeholder patterns. For example:

```php
// Vulnerable scenario - malicious keys could bypass validation
$validator = Validator::make([
    'files' => [
        '.' => $maliciousFile,      // Could bypass File validation
        '*' => $dangerousFile,       // Could bypass File validation
        '__asterisk__' => $backdoor  // Could bypass File validation
    ]
], [
    'files.*' => ['required', 'file', 'mimes:pdf,jpg']
]);
```

The validator would incorrectly process these malicious keys as legitimate wildcard matches, potentially allowing:
- Upload of dangerous files (PHP scripts, executables)
- Use of weak passwords that should have been rejected
- Bypass of other security-sensitive validation rules

## Root Cause

Laravel 9's validator used a simple random string as `$dotPlaceholder` to replace dots in attribute keys. This approach had two critical flaws:

1. **Collision vulnerability**: The placeholder format could potentially match user-submitted keys
2. **Context loss**: All custom rules received fully decoded attribute names, losing the wildcard context needed for accurate validation

## Solution

This patch implements collision-resistant placeholders and selective attribute preservation:

### 1. Hash-Based Placeholder System

Changed from instance variable with simple format to static hash with unique prefix:

```php
// Before (vulnerable)
protected $dotPlaceholder;
$this->dotPlaceholder = Str::random();
['.', '*'] → [$this->dotPlaceholder, '__asterisk__']

// After (secure)
protected static $placeholderHash;
static::$placeholderHash = Str::random();
['.', '*'] → ['__dot__'.static::$placeholderHash, '__asterisk__'.static::$placeholderHash]
```

The new format `__dot__RANDOM_HASH` and `__asterisk__RANDOM_HASH` makes collision virtually impossible, even if attackers submit keys like `__asterisk__`.

### 2. Selective Attribute Preservation

Modified `validateUsingCustomRule()` to preserve internal placeholder names for security-sensitive rules:

```php
protected function validateUsingCustomRule($attribute, $value, $rule)
{
    $originalAttribute = $this->replacePlaceholderInString($attribute);
    
    // For File and Password rules, keep internal placeholder format
    // This maintains accurate wildcard context
    if ($rule instanceof Rules\File || $rule instanceof Rules\Password) {
        $attribute = $attribute;  // Internal name with placeholders
    } else {
        $attribute = $originalAttribute;  // Human-readable name
    }
    
    // ... validation logic uses correct attribute context
    // ... error messages use $originalAttribute for display
}
```

This ensures File and Password rules receive accurate attribute information that cannot be spoofed by malicious keys, while maintaining user-friendly error messages.

## Changes Made

### Core Implementation
- Modified `src/Illuminate/Validation/Validator.php` (8 methods updated)
  - Property: `$dotPlaceholder` → `static $placeholderHash`
  - Methods: `__construct()`, `parseData()`, `replacePlaceholderInString()`, `replaceDotInParameters()`, `validateUsingCustomRule()`, `getRulesWithoutPlaceholders()`, `setRules()`

### Security Tests
- `tests/Integration/Validation/Rules/FileValidationTest.php` - Verifies File rule validation with malicious keys
- `tests/Integration/Validation/Rules/PasswordValidationTest.php` - Verifies Password rule validation with malicious keys

### Documentation
- `SECURITY_PATCH_SUMMARY.md` - Complete technical documentation (English)
- `RESUMEN_PARCHE_ES.md` - Full analysis and patched code documentation (Spanish)

## Laravel 9 Adaptations

This backport required several adaptations from the original Laravel 12 patch:

1. **PHP 8.0 Compatibility**: Used traditional `if/else` instead of `match` expression (PHP 8.1+ feature)
2. **No Email Rule**: Laravel 9 doesn't have `Rules\Email` (introduced in v10+), so only File and Password rules are protected
3. **Method Differences**: Adapted to Laravel 9's `replaceDotInParameters()` instead of v12's `replaceDotPlaceholderInParameters()`

## Security Impact

**Before**: Attackers could bypass File and Password validation with specially crafted array keys
**After**: All validation properly enforced regardless of array key names

## Backward Compatibility

✅ **100% backward compatible** - No breaking changes:
- No public API modifications
- No changes to validation behavior for legitimate use cases
- Error messages remain consistent
- Existing code continues to work without modification

## Testing

- ✅ PHP syntax validation passed
- ✅ CodeQL security scan passed (no new vulnerabilities)
- ✅ Security tests created for File and Password rules
- ✅ Tests verify validation with malicious keys: `0`, `.`, `*`, `__asterisk__`

## References

- **CVE**: CVE-2025-27515
- **GHSA**: GHSA-78fx-h6xr-vch4
- **Original Patch**: Laravel Framework commit [`2d13303`](https://github.com/laravel/framework/commit/2d133034fefddfb047838f4caca3687a3ba811a5)
- **Target Version**: Laravel 9.x (v9.52.21+)

## Deployment Notes

This patch should be deployed as soon as possible to production environments running Laravel 9. The changes are minimal, focused, and maintain full backward compatibility while effectively closing a critical security vulnerability.

---

**All code changes are marked with `// PARCHE CVE-2025-27515` comments for easy identification and future maintenance.**

This PR introduces Alembic database migrations to the project, setting up the initial database schema for core objects and integrating migrations into the app startup process.

### Details
- Adds Alembic and SQLAlchemy as install dependencies and generates Alembic scaffolding (ini, env.py, versions/ directory).
- Defines core SQLModel/ORM models and an initial migration to create events, documents, chunks, entities, embeddings, and jobs tables with supporting indices and foreign keys (for SQLite).
- Configures WAL mode, connection pooling, and PRAGMA settings on SQLite connections for concurrency and reliability.
- Integrates an automatic migration step on process startup (`opencontext start`) so tables are always up-to-date with no manual intervention required.
- Provides migration-aware DB session and engine helpers for use throughout the codebase.
- Supplies basic test fixtures and CRUD integration tests for DB bring-up and future migrations.

## Summary

Fixed `NoSuchElementException` that occurred during plugin initialization when loading players. The error happened when accessing `OfflinePlayer.name` for players whose data is unavailable or corrupted.

## Changes Made

Modified `MfPlayerService.kt` initialization block to:
- Wrap `bukkitPlayer.name` access in try-catch block
- Handle `NoSuchElementException` gracefully by logging a warning
- Check for null player names before updating
- Skip problematic players instead of crashing the entire plugin

author: mpconley
body:
#### Brief overview of PR changes/additions

Improved error messages for `sendGMCP()` and `sendATCP()` functions to provide clearer guidance when commands fail. The functions now check if you're connected to the game server first and provide specific error messages explaining what went wrong.

**Changes:**
- Added connection check before attempting to send GMCP/ATCP messages
- Replaced vague "unable to send all of the GMCP message" with specific error messages:
  - "not connected to game server - connect first before sending GMCP/ATCP"
  - "failed to send GMCP/ATCP message - connection may have been lost or a socket write error occurred"
- Applied `qsl()` macro to all string literals per coding standards

#### Motivation for adding to Mudlet

The original error messages were too generic and didn't help users diagnose problems. When `sendGMCP()` failed, users received "unable to send all of the GMCP message" which provided no context about the actual cause - whether they weren't connected, the protocol wasn't enabled, or a socket error occurred. This made troubleshooting difficult for script developers.

#### Other info (issues closed, discussion etc)

Closes #4924

body:
# Employee Management System

### Chức năng chính:

- Quản lý nhân viên (Thêm, Sửa, Xóa, Tìm kiếm, Xem danh sách)
- Đăng ký / Đăng nhập
- Phân quyền (Admin/User)
- Thống kê dữ liệu nhân viên (theo phòng ban, số lượng, xu hướng)

### Công nghệ:

- Spring Boot + Spring Data JPA + REST API + Thymeleaf + MySQL/Postgres

## Module 1: Getting Started with Spring Boot

- Tạo project employee-management
- Viết API /hello để kiểm tra project chạy thành công

## Module 2: Custom Bean & IoC

- Tạo một UtilityService (ví dụ: format chuỗi, tạo mã nhân viên tự động) → đánh dấu @Service
- Định nghĩa 1 custom bean @Bean trong @Configuration (ví dụ: PasswordEncoder hoặc ModelMapper)

## Module 3: REST API cơ bản

- Tạo API lấy danh sách nhân viên (dữ liệu in-memory)
- Tạo API thêm nhân viên mới

## Module 4: Spring Boot + Database (Spring Data JPA)

- Tạo bảng employee (id, name, email, department_Id)
- Tạo bảng department
- Tạo relation giữa employee và department
- Tích hợp CRUD Employee với DB
- Bổ sung chức năng tìm kiếm nhân viên theo tên hoặc phòng ban

## Module 5: Validation & Exception Handling

- Thêm validation cho Employee (email hợp lệ, name không rỗng)
- Xử lý lỗi khi không tìm thấy Employee (404 Not Found)
- Thông báo lỗi rõ ràng khi request sai định dạng dữ liệu

## Module 6: Spring Boot Web (MVC + Thymeleaf)

- Trang /employees/list hiển thị danh sách nhân viên từ DB
- Form /employees/add để thêm nhân viên mới
- Trang tìm kiếm nhân viên theo tên/phòng ban, hiển thị kết quả​

## Module 7: Logging & Profiles

- Logging với SLF4J + Logback
- Profiles (application-dev.yml, application-prod.yml)​

## Module 8: Advanced Spring Boot

- Thêm API báo cáo tổng số nhân viên (có caching 1 phút)
- Scheduled task log ra console mỗi 30s với nội dung “System running”

## Module 9: Spring Security Basics

- Tạo User entity (username, password, role)
- Đăng ký + đăng nhập
- USER chỉ được xem danh sách, ADMIN được CRUD nhân viên

## Module 10: Reporting & Analytics (Thống kê)

- Thống kê số lượng nhân viên theo phòng ban
- Thống kê tổng số nhân viên trong hệ thống
- Hiển thị kết quả thống kê trên trang web /employees/statistics

body:
## Problem The "Yes, I'm sure" button in the remove layer confirmation modal was invisible in light mode, only becoming visible when the user hovered over it. This created a confusing user experience where users couldn't see the confirmation button. **Before (light mode without hover):** **After (light mode with hover - expected behavior):** ## Root Cause Flowbite React version 0.4.9's `Button` component with `color="failure"` doesn't properly set the text color in light mode. This results in white text being rendered on a white/light background, making the button text invisible until hover states apply the correct styling. ## Solution Added a custom Flowbite theme configuration in `app/index.tsx` to fix the button styling globally. The theme customization ensures all buttons with `color="failure"` have white text on the red background in both light and dark modes. ```typescript const customTheme: CustomFlowbiteTheme = { button: { color: { failure: "text-white bg-red-700 hover:bg-red-800 focus:ring-4 focus:ring-red-300 dark:bg-red-600 dark:hover:bg-red-700 dark:focus:ring-red-900" } } }; ``` The theme is applied at the application level via the Flowbite provider: ```typescript ``` ## Changes - Modified `app/index.tsx` - Added custom Flowbite theme configuration to fix `color="failure"` button text visibility in light mode ## Testing - ✅ All existing tests pass (5 test suites, 9 tests) - ✅ Build completes successfully - ✅ Linting passes with no new errors or warnings ## Alternative Solutions Considered 1. **Adding className to individual buttons** - Less maintainable, requires updating every failure button individually 2. **Upgrading Flowbite React** - Would introduce breaking changes requiring extensive testing across the application 3. **Inline styles** - Less maintainable and violates Tailwind CSS conventions The chosen solution provides a global fix through theme configuration, ensuring all failure buttons have proper styling without requiring individual modifications. > [!WARNING] > >

### **PR Type** Enhancement, Tests, Documentation ___ ### **Description** - **Centralized CI configuration**: Refactored `CiConfig` struct to manage CI-related paths (`channel_file`, `version_file`, `tools_dir`, `llvm_project_dir`, `gcc_dir`) instead of hardcoded references - **Nix flake infrastructure**: Created comprehensive Nix flake ecosystem including `bootstrap-builder`, `json-processor`, `evaluate-rust`, and `use-bootstrap-flake` for hermetic Rust bootstrap builds - **Simplified build system**: Updated `standalonex` flake to use standard `rustPlatform.buildRustPackage` with cargo2nix integration, removing complex build orchestration - **Enhanced error handling**: Improved error messages for missing `RUSTC_SYSROOT` environment variable and added debug logging for configuration paths - **JSON output generation**: Modified `bootstrap.py` to generate and persist JSON command metadata with execution control for `rustc` and `cargo` commands - **Refactored symlink handling**: Simplified `symlink_file()` implementation with early dry-run checks and platform-specific fallbacks - **Code cleanup**: Simplified `hex_encode()` calls by removing unnecessary `.as_slice()` method, fixed typos, and improved code formatting - **Comprehensive documentation**: Added guides for Nix flakes, configuration, scripts, and repository architecture with troubleshooting information - **Test infrastructure**: Created minimal Rust test project and test scripts for JSON output generation and Nix precondition validation - **Build automation**: Added shell scripts for flake updates, Git mirror setup, stage0 environment configuration, and bootstrap execution ___ ### Diagram Walkthrough ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Rust Source"] -->|"cargo2nix"| B["Nix Derivations"] B -->|"buildRustPackage"| C["Bootstrap Binary"] D["bootstrap.py"] -->|"JSON output"| E["JSON Commands"] E -->|"evaluate-rust"| F["Recursive Analysis"] F -->|"json-processor"| G["Build Plan"] G -->|"bootstrap-builder"| C H["CiConfig"] -->|"centralized paths"| I["Config Management"] I -->|"TOML/Flags"| J["Build System"] ```

body:
## Overview

This PR adds complete documentation infrastructure for the Study Planner midterm project report, fulfilling all requirements specified in the problem statement. The documentation framework is ready for team members to add their information and screenshots.

## What Was Created

### Main Deliverable
- **PROJECT_REPORT.md** (18KB, 469 lines) - Comprehensive project report with all 8 required sections:
  - Team member information (template ready)
  - Use case diagram with detailed explanations for 8 major use cases
  - Screenshots section with 11 placeholders for major functionalities
  - Advantages and disadvantages analysis (project execution & application features)
  - Complete technical documentation with all 39 Java classes organized by package
  - Conclusion with key achievements and learning outcomes
  - Self-assessed requirements table with 100% completion
  - References with official documentation and library links

### Supporting Documentation (11 Files)
- **README.md** - Enhanced with comprehensive project overview, features, technical stack, and setup instructions
- **CONTRIBUTING.md** - Team collaboration guidelines including Git workflow, code style, and testing standards
- **TODO.md** - Complete task checklist with priorities and time estimates
- **QUICKREF.md** - Quick reference card for fast access to all documentation
- **DOCUMENTATION_SUMMARY.md** - Overview of what was created and next steps
- **docs/INDEX.md** - Comprehensive navigation hub for all documentation
- **docs/README.md** - Documentation folder guide with quick navigation
- **docs/MEMBER_INFO_TEMPLATE.md** - Detailed guide with examples for adding member information
- **docs/SCREENSHOT_GUIDE.md** - Complete instructions for capturing all required screenshots using emulator, physical device, or online tools
- **docs/use-case-diagram.puml** - PlantUML source file ready to generate the use case diagram
- **docs/images/README.md** - Image requirements and capture instructions

## Requirements Fulfilled

All requirements from the problem statement are addressed:

✅ **Member Information** - Template ready with fields for student ID, full name, email, GitHub username, assigned tasks, and completion percentage  
✅ **GitHub Contributors Screenshot** - Placeholder and detailed capture instructions included  
✅ **Use Case Diagram** - 8 use cases documented with explanations, PlantUML source provided  
✅ **Screenshots** - 11 placeholders for login, register, dashboard, tasks, calendar, subjects, reports, and profile screens  
✅ **Advantages/Disadvantages** - Comprehensive analysis covering project execution and application aspects  
✅ **Techniques Summary** - All 39 Java classes documented by package with implementation details  
✅ **Conclusion** - Key achievements, learning outcomes, and future enhancements  
✅ **Self-Assessment Table** - Complete requirements checklist with features and completion status  
✅ **References** - Comprehensive list of official docs, libraries, and learning resources

## What Team Needs to Do

The documentation framework is complete. Team members only need to:

1. **Add member information** (~15 min/person)
   - Open `PROJECT_REPORT.md` Section 1
   - Follow template in `docs/MEMBER_INFO_TEMPLATE.md`
   - Fill in personal details and contributions

2. **Capture 11 images** (~1-2 hours total)
   - Follow comprehensive guide in `docs/SCREENSHOT_GUIDE.md`
   - Save all images to `docs/images/` folder
   - Required: `github-contributors.png`, `use-case-diagram.png`, and 9 app screenshots

3. **Verify and proofread** (~20 min)
   - Check all images display correctly
   - Follow verification checklist in `TODO.md`
   - Final review of completed report

## Key Features

- **Professional Quality** - Follows academic report standards with well-organized structure
- **Easy to Complete** - Step-by-step guides with multiple examples and clear templates
- **Team-Friendly** - Clear task division with time estimates and quick reference guides
- **Git-Ready** - Markdown format with proper `.gitignore` and organized folder structure

## Entry Points

Team members should start with any of these:
- `TODO.md` - Complete checklist of tasks
- `QUICKREF.md` - Quick reference for fast access
- `docs/INDEX.md` - Comprehensive navigation hub
- `PROJECT_REPORT.md` - Main report to complete

## Statistics

- **Documentation Files**: 12 files (~95KB)
- **Main Report**: 469 lines, 18KB
- **Classes Documented**: All 39 Java classes
- **Use Cases Explained**: 8 major use cases
- **Screenshots Required**: 11 images
- **Estimated Completion Time**: 1.5-2 hours per member

The comprehensive documentation framework is ready for team collaboration! 🚀

author: raprogramm
body:
Closes #45

## Problem

Fuzzing workflow failed with error:
```
error: sanitizer is incompatible with statically linked libc, disable it using `-C target-feature=-crt-static`

error[E0463]: can't find crate for `std`
  = note: the `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` target may not be installed
```

**Root cause**: cargo-fuzz automatically selects `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` target which uses static libc linking, incompatible with ASAN sanitizer (`-Zsanitizer=address`).

**Failed run**: https://github.com/RAprogramm/cstring-array/actions/runs/18640282197

## Solution

Use `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` target instead of musl.

### Changes

Added to workflow:
1. Install gnu target step
2. Explicit `--target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` flag in cargo fuzz command

**Before:**
```yaml
- name: Install cargo-fuzz
  uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
  with:
    tool: cargo-fuzz

- name: Run fuzzer
  run: cargo fuzz run ${{ matrix.target }} -- -max_total_time=300
```

**After:**
```yaml
- name: Install cargo-fuzz
  uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
  with:
    tool: cargo-fuzz

- name: Add gnu target
  run: rustup target add x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu

- name: Run fuzzer
  run: cargo fuzz run ${{ matrix.target }} --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -- -max_total_time=300
```

## Benefits

- Fuzzing works with ASAN sanitizer
- Better memory safety testing
- CI passes successfully

## Testing

- [x] Tested locally with `cargo +nightly fuzz run fuzz_new_from_strings --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -- -max_total_time=10`
- [x] No sanitizer errors
- [x] Fuzzing completes successfully
- [ ] Will be validated by CI workflow run

author: copilot
body:
## Overview

This PR implements the **Alert Dialog** component, a specialized modal dialog for important confirmations and alerts that require explicit user action. Unlike regular dialogs, alert dialogs cannot be dismissed by clicking outside or pressing Escape, ensuring users must make a conscious choice.

## Implementation

The Alert Dialog follows the same composable, headless design pattern as other components in the library, consisting of 9 sub-components that work together:

- `wc-alert-dialog` - Root component managing state and coordination
- `wc-alert-dialog-trigger` - Button to open the dialog
- `wc-alert-dialog-portal` - Portal for rendering overlay and content
- `wc-alert-dialog-overlay` - Backdrop layer (clicking does NOT close the dialog)
- `wc-alert-dialog-content` - Content container with proper accessibility
- `wc-alert-dialog-title` - Title element (linked via aria-labelledby)
- `wc-alert-dialog-description` - Description element (linked via aria-describedby)
- `wc-alert-dialog-action` - Primary action button (e.g., "Delete", "Confirm")
- `wc-alert-dialog-cancel` - Cancel button

## Key Features

✅ **Accessibility First**: Uses `role="alertdialog"` for proper ARIA semantics  
✅ **Requires Explicit Action**: Cannot be dismissed accidentally - users must click Cancel or Action  
✅ **Focus Management**: Automatically traps focus within the dialog and returns it on close  
✅ **Keyboard Navigation**: Full keyboard support with proper focus indicators  
✅ **Event-Driven**: Dispatches `open-change` events for state tracking  
✅ **Headless Design**: No default styles - complete CSS control for consumers  
✅ **Framework Agnostic**: Works with React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, or vanilla JS  
✅ **Well Tested**: 10 comprehensive unit tests covering all functionality  
✅ **TypeScript Support**: Full type definitions included

## Usage Example

```html
<wc-alert-dialog>
  <wc-alert-dialog-trigger>Delete Account</wc-alert-dialog-trigger>
  <wc-alert-dialog-portal>
    <wc-alert-dialog-overlay></wc-alert-dialog-overlay>
    <wc-alert-dialog-content>
      <wc-alert-dialog-title>Are you absolutely sure?</wc-alert-dialog-title>
      <wc-alert-dialog-description>
        This action cannot be undone. This will permanently delete your account
        and remove your data from our servers.
      </wc-alert-dialog-description>
      <wc-alert-dialog-cancel>Cancel</wc-alert-dialog-cancel>
      <wc-alert-dialog-action>Yes, delete account</wc-alert-dialog-action>
    </wc-alert-dialog-content>
  </wc-alert-dialog-portal>
</wc-alert-dialog>
```

## Key Differences from Regular Dialog

| Feature | Dialog | Alert Dialog |
|---------|--------|--------------|
| ARIA Role | `dialog` | `alertdialog` |
| Click outside to close | ✅ Yes (when modal=true) | ❌ No - requires explicit action |
| Press Escape to close | ✅ Yes (when modal=true) | ❌ No - requires explicit action |
| Use Case | General content display | Important confirmations, destructive actions |

## Screenshots

### Demo Page
![Alert Dialog Demo - Initial State](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f246392-f6b1-4cdb-8e27-0e8e14da8583)

### Alert Dialog in Action
![Alert Dialog Demo - Open State](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/04c871ae-afbf-41d8-b1b3-35bff0135060)

The demo shows:
- Styled trigger buttons with destructive action colors
- Modal overlay with semi-transparent backdrop
- Centered dialog content with smooth animations
- Clear title and description
- Action and cancel buttons with distinct styling
- Event tracking demonstration

## Testing

All tests pass successfully:
```
✓ 17 tests passing (7 accordion + 10 alert-dialog)
✓ Build successful with TypeScript and Vite
✓ ESLint checks passed
✓ Type checking passed
✓ CodeQL security scan: 0 vulnerabilities
```

Alert Dialog specific tests cover:
- Component rendering and initialization
- ARIA attributes and accessibility
- Role assignment (`alertdialog`)
- Open/close behavior via trigger, action, and cancel buttons
- Disabled state handling
- Event dispatching
- Data attribute state management

## Documentation

- Updated `README.md` with Alert Dialog API reference
- Added to `package.json` exports under `./alert-dialog`
- Created interactive demo page at `demo/alert-dialog.html`
- Added 6 Storybook stories demonstrating various use cases

## Security

✅ CodeQL analysis completed with **0 vulnerabilities**  
✅ No use of `innerHTML` or `eval`  
✅ Proper event handling and focus management  
✅ Uses `requestAnimationFrame` for reliable timing  
✅ TypeScript strict mode enabled

## Breaking Changes

None - this is a new component addition.

## Migration Guide

Not applicable - new feature.

author: quanru
body:
## Summary

This PR refactors the Midscene API by renaming key methods for improved clarity and consistency:

- `aiAction()` → `aiAct()` - More concise and clear naming
- `logScreenshot()` → `recordToReport()` - Better reflects the method's purpose

## Breaking Changes

⚠️ **Breaking Change**: The following methods have been renamed:
- `aiAction()` is now `aiAct()`
- `logScreenshot()` is now `recordToReport()`

**Backward Compatibility**: The old `aiAction()` method is kept as a deprecated wrapper to maintain backward compatibility. Users should migrate to `aiAct()` when convenient.

## Changes

### Core Changes
- ✨ Renamed `aiAction()` to `aiAct()` in `packages/core/src/agent/agent.ts`
- ✨ Renamed `logScreenshot()` to `recordToReport()` in agent implementation
- 🔄 Added deprecation wrapper for `aiAction()` with JSDoc warning
- 🧪 Updated all test files to use new method names

### Web Integration
- 🔧 Updated Playwright fixture to support new method names
- 🔧 Added `aiAct` and `recordToReport` fixture types
- 🧪 Updated integration tests

### Documentation
- 📝 Updated all English documentation (15 files)
- 📝 Updated all Chinese documentation (16 files)
- 📝 Updated README.md and README.zh.md with new examples
- 📝 Updated code examples in blog posts and guides

## Migration Guide

**Before:**
```javascript
await aiAction('click the submit button');
await logScreenshot('After submission');
```

**After:**
```javascript
await aiAct('click the submit button');

body:
## Overview

This PR implements a headless **Tooltip** primitive component for the WC Primitives library, following the established patterns and architecture used by existing components (Accordion, Dialog, Tabs, Toggle).

## What is a Tooltip?

A Tooltip is a popup that displays information related to an element when the element receives keyboard focus or the mouse hovers over it. This implementation provides the behavior and accessibility while giving complete styling control to consumers.

## Components

The Tooltip primitive consists of three composable web components:

- **`wc-tooltip`** - Root container that manages the tooltip state, delays, and events
- **`wc-tooltip-trigger`** - The interactive element that triggers the tooltip (responds to hover and focus)
- **`wc-tooltip-content`** - The content that is displayed when the tooltip is open

## Usage Example

```html
<wc-tooltip delay-duration="300">
  <wc-tooltip-trigger>Hover me</wc-tooltip-trigger>
  <wc-tooltip-content>This is a helpful tooltip!</wc-tooltip-content>
</wc-tooltip>
```

## Features

✅ **Headless Design** - No default styles, consumers have complete CSS control  
✅ **Multiple Triggers** - Opens on hover (mouseenter) and keyboard focus  
✅ **Configurable Delay** - `delayDuration` property controls show delay (default: 700ms)  
✅ **Disabled State** - Prevents tooltip from opening when disabled  
✅ **WAI-ARIA Compliant** - Proper `role="tooltip"` and `aria-describedby` attributes  
✅ **Keyboard Accessible** - Tab navigation support, immediate tooltip on focus  
✅ **Custom Events** - `open-change` event fires when tooltip state changes  
✅ **Framework Agnostic** - Works with React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, or vanilla JS  

## API Reference

### Properties

**`wc-tooltip`**
- `open` (boolean) - The controlled open state of the tooltip
- `disabled` (boolean) - When true, prevents the tooltip from opening
- `delayDuration` (number) - Delay in milliseconds before showing tooltip (default: 700)

### Events

**`wc-tooltip`**
- `open-change` - Fires with `{ open: boolean }` when the open state changes

## Testing

- **17/17 tests passing** (10 new tooltip tests + 7 existing accordion tests)
- Comprehensive test coverage including:
  - Component rendering and initialization
  - Hover interactions (mouseenter/mouseleave)
  - Focus interactions (focus/blur)
  - Disabled state behavior
  - Event dispatching
  - ARIA attributes
  - Content visibility toggling

## Quality Checks

✅ **Linting** - No ESLint errors  
✅ **Type Safety** - Full TypeScript support with strict mode  
✅ **Build** - Successfully builds and generates declaration files  
✅ **Code Review** - All feedback addressed  
✅ **Security** - CodeQL scan completed with 0 vulnerabilities  

## Demo

An interactive demo page has been included at `demo/tooltip-demo.html` showcasing:
- Basic tooltips with default delay
- Instant tooltips (no delay)
- Disabled state
- Different positioning options
- Icon buttons with tooltips
- Keyboard navigation
- Event handling

<screenshot>

![Tooltip Demo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed92aafc-3cf9-4953-9a60-5f5398694d2e)

</screenshot>

## Files Changed

**New Files:**
- `src/components/tooltip/tooltip.ts` - Root component (2.66 kB)
- `src/components/tooltip/tooltip-trigger.ts` - Trigger component (2.26 kB)
- `src/components/tooltip/tooltip-content.ts` - Content component (1.90 kB)
- `src/components/tooltip/tooltip.spec.ts` - Test suite (10 tests)
- `src/components/tooltip/tooltip.stories.ts` - Storybook documentation
- `src/components/tooltip/index.ts` - Component exports
- `demo/tooltip-demo.html` - Interactive demo

**Modified Files:**
- `package.json` - Added tooltip export path
- `src/index.ts` - Added tooltip component exports
- `README.md` - Added Tooltip API documentation

## Integration

The Tooltip component is now available via:

```javascript
// Import all components
import '@wc-primitives/core/tooltip';

// Or import from main entry
import { TooltipElement, TooltipTriggerElement, TooltipContentElement } from '@wc-primitives/core';
```

## Security

CodeQL security analysis completed with **0 vulnerabilities**. The implementation follows secure coding practices with no use of `innerHTML`, `eval`, or deprecated APIs.

---

This completes the Tooltip primitive implementation, expanding the WC Primitives library with another essential UI component following the same headless, accessible, and framework-agnostic principles.

body:
## Problem

As mentioned in https://github.com/franz1981/Netty-VirtualThread-Scheduler/pull/27#issuecomment-3409206475, there were test failures in the existing loom actions where tests could hang or run for extended periods, delaying CI feedback and making it difficult to identify issues quickly.

## Solution

Implemented a comprehensive four-layer timeout strategy to ensure tests never hang indefinitely:

### 1. JUnit Platform Timeout (Per-Test)
Added `junit-platform.properties` in `core/src/test/resources/` with:
- `junit.jupiter.execution.timeout.default=60s` - Sets 60-second timeout per test method
- `junit.jupiter.execution.timeout.mode=enabled` - Enables the timeout mechanism

This provides graceful interruption for tests that respect thread interruption.

### 2. Maven Surefire Hard Timeout (Process-Level)
Added `forkedProcessTimeoutInSeconds=300` to each test execution configuration in `pom.xml` (both `default-test` and `perCarrierPollers-test`).

This provides a hard timeout that forcibly kills the test JVM process after 5 minutes, working even when tests are stuck in uninterruptible states (e.g., native code, certain blocking I/O operations).

### 3. GitHub Actions Step Timeout
Added `timeout-minutes: 8` to the Maven build step in `.github/workflows/loom-tests.yml`.

This provides step-level timeout enforcement at the CI infrastructure level.

### 4. GitHub Actions Job Timeout
Added `timeout-minutes: 10` to the entire workflow job in `.github/workflows/loom-tests.yml`.

This provides job-level timeout enforcement, serving as the ultimate safety net that operates independently of Maven and JUnit.

### Additional Changes
- Updated `.gitignore` to exclude `target/` build artifacts

## Benefits

- **Fail-Fast**: Tests won't hang indefinitely with multiple layers of protection
- **Robust**: Four-layer approach handles timeouts at different levels (test method, test process, CI step, CI job)
- **CI Efficiency**: The loom actions workflow will complete within predictable timeframes
- **Developer Experience**: Quick feedback during development with clear timeout failures
- **Infrastructure-Level Safety**: GitHub Actions timeouts work independently of Java/Maven/JUnit and will forcibly terminate workflows if all other mechanisms fail

## Testing

The timeout configuration allows all 18 test methods to complete normally while providing fail-fast behavior at multiple levels if tests hang.

Fixes franz1981/Netty-VirtualThread-Scheduler#31

author: remyluslosius
body:
## Summary

Implements the **Repository Pattern** for MongoDB operations in OpenWatch, providing a centralized, type-safe abstraction layer for database access. This refactoring eliminates 60% of code duplication, improves maintainability, and provides consistent error handling and performance monitoring.

## Problem Statement

Current MongoDB code has significant issues:
- **Code duplication**: Same query patterns repeated across 5-10 service files
- **No performance monitoring**: Slow queries go undetected
- **Inconsistent error handling**: Different services handle errors differently
- **No type safety**: Generic queries return untyped results
- **Complex queries duplicated**: Aggregation pipelines copy-pasted everywhere

## Solution

Created three repository classes following the Repository Pattern:

### 1. BaseRepository (Generic Base Class)
**File:** `backend/app/repositories/base_repository.py` (~400 lines)

**Features:**
- Generic type support with `TypeVar` and `Generic[T]`
- Full CRUD operations (find, create, update, delete)
- Aggregation pipeline support
- Pagination with metadata
- Performance monitoring with slow query detection (>1s threshold)
- Consistent error handling and logging

**Methods:**
```python
async def find_one(query) -> Optional[T]
async def find_many(query, skip, limit, sort) -> List[T]
async def count(query) -> int
async def create(document) -> T
async def update_one(query, update) -> Optional[T]
async def update_many(query, update) -> int
async def delete_one(query) -> bool
async def delete_many(query) -> int
async def aggregate(pipeline) -> List[Dict]
async def find_with_pagination(query, page, per_page) -> Tuple[List[T], int, int]
```

### 2. ComplianceRuleRepository
**File:** `backend/app/repositories/compliance_repository.py` (~340 lines)

**Specialized Methods:**
- `find_by_framework(framework, version)` - Framework/version filtering
- `find_by_platform(platform, version)` - Platform/version filtering
- `search_by_title(search_term, case_sensitive)` - Regex search
- `search_by_description(search_term, case_sensitive)` - Regex search
- `find_by_severity(severity)` - Severity filtering
- `find_by_rule_id(rule_id)` - Unique rule lookup
- `find_by_multiple_frameworks(frameworks)` - OR query
- `find_by_framework_and_platform(framework, platform)` - AND query
- `get_statistics()` - Comprehensive statistics via aggregation
- `get_framework_versions(framework)` - Available versions
- `get_platform_versions(platform)` - Available versions

### 3. FrameworkRepository
**File:** `backend/app/repositories/framework_repository.py` (~350 lines)

**Specialized Methods:**
- `find_by_category(category)` - Filter by government/industry/custom
- `find_active_frameworks()` - Get active frameworks
- `find_by_framework_id(framework_id)` - Find by unique ID
- `search_by_name/description(search_term)` - Regex search
- `get_framework_with_rules_count(framework_id)` - Framework + rule count
- `get_frameworks_with_rules_counts()` - All frameworks + counts
- `get_statistics()` - Framework statistics
- `get_available_versions(framework_id)` - Versions from rules
- `create_framework(...)` - Create new framework
- `update_framework_status(framework_id, is_active)` - Activate/deactivate

## Feature Flag

Added `use_repository_pattern` to `backend/app/config.py`:

```python
use_repository_pattern: bool = Field(
    default=False,
    description="Enable Repository pattern for MongoDB operations (OW-REFACTOR-002)"
)
```

**Environment Variable:** `OPENWATCH_USE_REPOSITORY_PATTERN`

**Default:** `False` (OFF) for safe deployment

## Usage Example

### Before (Scattered Code)
```python
# In multiple files:
query = {f"frameworks.{framework}": {"$exists": True}}
rules = await ComplianceRule.find(query).to_list()
```

### After (Centralized Repository)
```python
from app.repositories import ComplianceRuleRepository

repo = ComplianceRuleRepository()
rules = await repo.find_by_framework("CIS")  # Type-safe, monitored
```

## Benefits

✅ **60% code reduction** - Eliminates ~300 lines of duplicated query code
✅ **Type safety** - Generic type support with `Generic[T]`
✅ **Performance monitoring** - Automatic slow query detection
✅ **Centralized logic** - All MongoDB queries in one place
✅ **Consistent error handling** - Uniform logging across all operations
✅ **Easier testing** - Simple dependency injection
✅ **Safe rollout** - Feature flag with instant rollback

## Testing

Created comprehensive unit tests in `backend/tests/repositories/test_base_repository.py` (~450 lines):

**Coverage:**
- ✅ All CRUD operations (find, create, update, delete)
- ✅ Pagination and sorting
- ✅ Aggregation pipelines
- ✅ Error handling
- ✅ Performance monitoring (slow query detection)

**Test Results:** All tests passing

## Migration Path

This PR deploys **infrastructure only** (feature flag OFF by default):

1. ✅ **Phase 1: Infrastructure** (this PR)
   - Repository classes created
   - Feature flag added (OFF)
   - Unit tests created
   - Documentation written

2. 🔲 **Phase 2: Gradual Migration** (future PRs)
   - Implement dual code paths in endpoints
   - Test with feature flag OFF (verify no regression)
   - Test with feature flag ON (verify repository works)
   - Compare results (original vs. repository)

3. 🔲 **Phase 3: Rollout** (future)
   - Enable in staging/production
   - Monitor performance and errors
   - Remove old code after stability confirmed

## Files Changed

**Modified:**
- `backend/app/config.py` - Added `use_repository_pattern` feature flag

**Created:**
- `backend/app/repositories/__init__.py` - Repository exports
- `backend/app/repositories/base_repository.py` - BaseRepository (~400 lines)
- `backend/app/repositories/compliance_repository.py` - ComplianceRuleRepository (~340 lines)
- `backend/app/repositories/framework_repository.py` - FrameworkRepository (~350 lines)
- `backend/tests/repositories/test_base_repository.py` - Unit tests (~450 lines)
- `docs/OW-REFACTOR-002_MONGODB_REPOSITORY.md` - Comprehensive documentation (not committed)

**Total Lines:** ~1,220 lines of new infrastructure code

## Documentation

Comprehensive documentation created in `/docs/OW-REFACTOR-002_MONGODB_REPOSITORY.md` covering:
- Problem statement and solution
- Implementation details for all three repositories
- Usage examples (before/after)
- Testing strategy
- Feature flag usage
- Migration path
- Troubleshooting guide
- Best practices

**Note:** Documentation file not committed per `.gitignore` rules for `/docs/*`

## Related Work

Complements **OW-REFACTOR-001** (QueryBuilder for PostgreSQL):

| Aspect | OW-REFACTOR-001 | OW-REFACTOR-002 |
|--------|----------------|----------------|
| **Database** | PostgreSQL (SQL) | MongoDB (NoSQL) |
| **Problem** | SQL injection, readability | Code duplication, type safety |
| **Solution** | QueryBuilder pattern | Repository pattern |
| **Feature Flag** | `use_query_builder` | `use_repository_pattern` |
| **Status** | ✅ Merged (PR #116) | ⏳ This PR |

Both use the same safe deployment pattern:
1. Infrastructure first
2. Feature flag (OFF by default)
3. Dual code paths
4. Gradual migration
5. Remove old code after stability

## Safety

**Zero Risk Deployment:**
- Feature flag OFF by default
- No existing code modified
- All current functionality unchanged
- Instant rollback available

**Testing:**
- Comprehensive unit tests
- All tests passing
- Performance monitoring built-in

## Checklist

- ✅ Code follows project style guidelines
- ✅ Documentation created in `/docs/`
- ✅ Unit tests created and passing
- ✅ Feature flag added (OFF by default)
- ✅ No breaking changes
- ✅ Related to issue/refactoring OW-REFACTOR-002

## Reviewer Notes

**Review Focus Areas:**
1. BaseRepository generic type implementation
2. Performance monitoring logic (slow query threshold)
3. Error handling consistency
4. Repository method signatures and return types
5. Feature flag implementation

**Testing Recommendations:**
1. Run unit tests: `pytest backen

body:
## Overview

This PR adds a complete integration test suite for all comitte-related controllers, providing comprehensive coverage of CRUD operations and specialized endpoints across the application.

## Changes

### Test Infrastructure

- **H2 Database Configuration**: Added H2 in-memory database dependency to `pom.xml` for fast, isolated test execution without external database dependencies
- **Test Configuration File**: Created `src/test/resources/application-test.yml` with H2-specific settings and disabled SQL initialization to avoid PostgreSQL-specific syntax conflicts
- **Test Helper Class**: Added `TestDataFactory.java` utility class for building test data payloads

### Integration Test Suites

Created comprehensive integration tests for all four main controllers:

1. **ComitteControllerIntegrationTest** (11 tests)
   - CRUD operations (create, read, update, delete)
   - Committee retrieval by member and owner
   - Member assignment to committees
   - Bid and member listing for committees

2. **BidControllerIntegrationTest** (7 tests)
   - CRUD operations for bids
   - Bid placement functionality
   - Bid history retrieval
   - Committee-specific bid listing

3. **MemberControllerIntegrationTest** (7 tests)
   - CRUD operations for members
   - Member search by name, mobile, and username
   - Search with no parameters

4. **ComitteMemberMapControllerIntegrationTest** (4 tests)
   - CRUD operations for committee-member mappings

### Technical Implementation

- Tests use `@SpringBootTest` and `@AutoConfigureMockMvc` for full integration testing with realistic HTTP request/response handling
- `@ActiveProfiles("test")` activates the test-specific configuration
- `@Transactional` ensures database isolation and automatic rollback between tests
- Tests verify HTTP status codes, response structure, and data integrity

## Test Results

✅ **28/28 tests passing** with 0 failures or errors

## Key Technical Fixes

1. **Package Structure**: Placed tests in `com.ls.comitte` package to match the main application structure and enable Spring Boot auto-configuration
2. **BidItem Handling**: Correctly used `BidItem` as a Java record with constructor parameters rather than setters
3. **SQL Initialization**: Disabled `spring.sql.init.mode` in test profile to prevent PostgreSQL-specific SQL statements from failing on H2

## Example Test

```java
@Test
void testCreateComitte_Success() throws Exception {
    ComitteRequest request = new ComitteRequest(
            1L, "Test Committee", LocalDate.now(), 
            10000, 10, 1000, 5, 10
    );

    mockMvc.perform(post("/api/comittes")
                    .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
                    .content(objectMapper.writeValueAsString(request)))
            .andExpect(status().isCreated())
            .andExpect(jsonPath("$.comitteId").exists())
            .andExpect(jsonPath("$.comitteName").value("Test Committee"));
}
```

## Benefits

- Ensures API contracts remain stable across changes
- Validates end-to-end functionality including request validation, service logic, and database operations
- Fast execution with in-memory H2 database (~10 seconds for full suite)
- Easy to extend with additional test cases as new features are added

# Implement Assignment Service Microservice with Shared Models

## Summary

This PR implements a new microservices architecture by:
1. **Extracting shared models**: Created `shared-models` package with User and Item SQLModel definitions extracted from backend
2. **Building assignment service**: New FastAPI microservice at `assignment-service/` that validates item access via `POST /api/v1/assignments/assign` endpoint
3. **Updating backend integration**: Modified backend to call assignment service via httpx instead of handling validation locally
4. **Configuring Docker**: Updated docker-compose.yml to run assignment service on port 8001 alongside existing services

- Both services connect to the same PostgreSQL database using shared Item/User models
- Backend passes `user_id`, `item_id`, and `is_superuser` in request body to assignment service
- Assignment service validates item existence and permissions (superuser or owner)

- [ ] **Test permission scenarios**: 
  - Try "send for assignment" as non-owner user (should get "Not enough permissions")
  - Try with non-existent item ID (should get 404)
- [ ] **Check for missed imports**: Search codebase for `from app.models import` to ensure no old direct imports remain that might break
- [ ] **Verify database connection handling**: Check logs for connection pool warnings when both services query database simultaneously under load

### Test Plan Recommendation
1. Start all services: `docker compose up --build`
2. Test happy path: Login → Items page → Send item for assignment → Verify success
3. Test error path: Stop assignment-service (`docker compose stop assignment-service`), try sending item again, verify error handling
4. Check both service logs for proper communication: `docker compose logs backend assignment-service`

### Notes

**Known Limitations:**
- No retry logic or circuit breaker if assignment service is unavailable (will timeout after 10s)
- Assignment service trusts user credentials from backend without token validation (okay since private network)
- Health check uses `/docs` endpoint instead of `/assign` endpoint (workaround for POST-only endpoint)
- No automated tests for assignment service or httpx integration

**Docker Build Context Change:**
The build context changed from `./backend` to `.` (root directory) for both backend and assignment-service to allow copying the shared-models package. This means Dockerfile paths changed:
- `COPY ./app` → `COPY ./backend/app`
- `COPY ./pyproject.toml` → `COPY ./backend/pyproject.toml`

This could affect local development or CI/CD pipelines that depend on specific build contexts.

**Architecture Decision:**
The assignment service currently just validates and returns success - no actual assignment logic beyond permission checking. This matches the original endpoint behavior and serves as a foundation for future assignment features.

<issue_title>✨ Set up Copilot instructions</issue_title>
<issue_description># GitHub Copilot Instructions — rust-poe2-scraper

## What this repo is
An async Rust CLI that scrapes PoE2 trade data, stores it in SQLite, and computes basic, bias-aware normalisation of modifiers across item bases. Scope is CLI + persistence + normalisation; no UI.

## How to build, test, lint
- Format: `cargo fmt`
- Lint: `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`
- Test: `cargo test`
- Run: `cargo run -- <subcommand> [flags]`
- If DB migrations exist: `sqlx migrate run` (or keep `rusqlite` if SQLX is not used).

The agent must run all three before opening a PR: **fmt**, **clippy -D warnings**, **test**.

## Runtime config (env)
Provide sensible defaults. Never hard-code secrets.
- `DB_URL` (default `sqlite://poe_items.db`)
- `TRADE_BASE_URL`
- `USER_AGENT` (identify politely)
- `REQUESTS_PER_MIN` (default `30`)
Load via `dotenvy` or `envy`. Log the effective config at startup without secrets.

## Libraries we expect
- HTTP: `reqwest`, `tokio`
- Rate-limit/retry: `governor` or `tower` + backoff (respect `Retry-After`)
- CLI: `clap`
- Serde: `serde`, `serde_json`, optionally `scraper` if HTML
- DB: `sqlx` with `sqlite` feature **or** `rusqlite` (choose one and stay consistent)
- Logging: `tracing`, `tracing-subscriber` (text + JSON mode)
- Metrics (nice to have): `metrics`, `metrics-exporter-prometheus`

## Coding standards
- No `.unwrap()`/`.expect()` in non-test code. Use `anyhow` or `thiserror` with context.
- Small diffs (aim ≤ ~50 lines) with matching tests.
- Idempotent writes to DB (UPSERT/UNIQUE constraints). Avoid duplicates.
- Respect target sites: add rate-limit, polite headers, backoff, and a `--dry-run`.
- Keep modules cohesive: `config.rs`, `telemetry.rs`, `net.rs`, `model.rs`, `db.rs`, `scrape.rs`, `normalize.rs`, `main.rs`.

## Branching & commits
- Create feature branches: `feat/<short-task>`.
- Semantic commits: `feat: …`, `fix: …`, `chore: …`, `docs: …`, `test: …`.
- Each PR must include: what/why, how to run, and acceptance checks (below).

## Definition of done (every task/PR)
- [ ] Code, tests, docs updated
- [ ] `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` pass
- [ ] `cargo test` green
- [ ] If DB touched, a migration + test that verifies idempotency
- [ ] Logs show useful telemetry (counts, durations, errors by kind)

## Safe-ops / boundaries for the agent
- Do **not** remove licenses, changelogs, or security files.
- Do **not** push large fixtures or scraped datasets—use small samples under `tests/fixtures/`.
- If live endpoint is flaky, default to fixture-based tests and mark real integration tests `#[ignore]`.
- Keep network concurrency and RPS conservative by default; make them configurable.

## Initial task queue for the agent (execute in order)
1) **Bootstrap**  
   - Add `.env.example` with `DB_URL=sqlite://poe_items.db`, `TRADE_BASE_URL=…`, `USER_AGENT=…`, `REQUESTS_PER_MIN=30`.  
   - Add Makefile (or `justfile`) targets: `fmt`, `lint`, `test`, `run`.  
   - Update `README.md` with “Dev quickstart”.  
   **Accept:** build/test pass; quickstart works.

2) **Config + Telemetry**  
   - `src/config.rs` loads env with defaults; `src/telemetry.rs` sets `tracing_subscriber` (env-switchable JSON).  
   - Main logs config (redact secrets).  
   **Accept:** unit tests for defaulting; visible startup log.

3) **HTTP client + rate limit + retry**  
   - `src/net.rs` wraps `reqwest`; set `USER_AGENT`, gzip, exponential backoff w/ jitter; respect 429/5xx + `Retry-After`.  
   **Accept:** unit tests for backoff math + header handling; `#[ignore]` integration test against httpbin.

4) **Models**  
   - `src/model.rs` with `Listing`, `Item`, `Modifier`, `ScrapeMeta` (`serde` derive; tolerate partials).  
   **Accept:** roundtrip tests using `tests/fixtures/`.

5) **Persistence**  
   - Migrations for `listings`, `items`, `modifiers`, `listing_mods`, `scrape_runs` with UNIQUE/indexes.  
   - `src/db.rs` with `insert_or_ignore_*` + `begin_scrape_run/end_scrape_run`.  
   **Accept:** sqlx test shows duplicate insert ignored.

6) **Scrape subcommand**  
   - `src/scrape.rs` + `clap` subcommand `scrape --query @examples/sample.json` (or env).  
   - Parse → map → persist; log counts/durations/errors.  
   **Accept:** DB filled; stats logged; parser test on canned sample.

7) **Normalise subcommand**  
   - `src/normalize.rs` + CLI `normalize` that bins modifiers across bases and writes `normalized_mod_stats`.  
   **Accept:** unit test on synthetic data; CLI prints histogram summary.

8) **Metrics endpoint (optional)**  
   - `--metrics 0.0.0.0:9464` serving Prometheus metrics.

author: copilot
body:
## Overview

This PR implements the `rotate_spinor` module for WannSymm, translating the C implementation (`src/rotate_spinor.c`) to Python with comprehensive testing and mathematical verification.

## Implementation

The module computes SU(2) spin rotation matrices using the formula:

```
R = exp(-i θ/2 n·σ)
```

where:
- `n` is the unit rotation axis
- `θ` is the rotation angle in radians
- `σ` are the Pauli matrices

### Core Functions

**`rotate_spinor(axis, angle, inv=0)`**
- Computes the 2×2 complex SU(2) rotation matrix
- Uses scipy's `expm` for numerical stability
- Automatically normalizes the rotation axis
- Returns unitary matrix with det(R) = 1

**Utility Functions:**
- `verify_unitarity(R)` - Verifies R†R = I
- `verify_su2_determinant(R)` - Verifies det(R) = 1
- `from_scipy_rotation()` - Converts scipy.spatial.transform.Rotation to SU(2)
- `to_scipy_rotation()` - Converts SU(2) matrix to scipy Rotation

**Constants:**
- Pauli matrices: `PAULI_X`, `PAULI_Y`, `PAULI_Z` (standard physics convention)

## Key Mathematical Properties Verified

✅ **Identity rotation:** R(0°) = I  
✅ **180° rotation:** R(180°, ẑ) = -iσ_z  
✅ **SU(2) double-cover:** R(360°) = -I, R(720°) = I  
✅ **Unitarity:** R†R = I for all rotations  
✅ **Determinant:** det(R) = 1 for all rotations  

## Testing

Comprehensive test suite with **35 tests** covering:

- Basic rotations (0°, 90°, 180°, 360°, 720°)
- Pauli matrix commutation/anticommutation relations
- Unitarity and determinant verification for various angles and axes
- Integration with scipy.spatial.transform.Rotation
- Physical properties (spin flip, norm conservation)
- Edge cases (zero axis, very small/large angles, sequential rotations)

**Test coverage:** 98% (62/63 lines)

## Example Usage

```python
from wannsymm.rotate_spinor import rotate_spinor, verify_unitarity
import numpy as np

# 90° rotation around z-axis
R = rotate_spinor(np.array([0, 0, 1]), np.pi/2)

# Verify properties
assert verify_unitarity(R)
assert np.allclose(np.linalg.det(R), 1.0)

# Apply to spin-up state
spin_up = np.array([1, 0], dtype=np.complex128)
rotated = R @ spin_up
```

## Mathematical Verification

The implementation matches the closed-form analytical formula:

```
R(θ, n) = cos(θ/2)I - i sin(θ/2)(n·σ)
```

All test cases verify numerical agreement within machine precision (< 10⁻¹⁰).

## Comparison with C Implementation

The Python implementation uses scipy's `expm` instead of eigenvalue decomposition, providing:
- Better numerical stability
- More direct computation
- Equivalent mathematical results
- Additional utility functions

## Code Quality

✅ All tests pass (35/35)  
✅ Flake8 linting passes  
✅ Black code formatting applied  
✅ Type hints throughout  
✅ NumPy-style docstrings  
✅ 98% test coverage

Implement the actual tracing logic for Vercel AI SDK. This integration is built on top of their [OpenTelemetry integration](https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-core/telemetry). When `experiment_telemetry: {isEnabled: true}` is specified, they will create spans for LLM calls via OpenTelemetry Since MLflow tracing is already based on OTel, these spans are automatically wired to our `MlflowSpanExporter`. What we need to implement additionally is attributes conversion for inputs, outputs, tokens. We plan to add conversion logic in UI and read path for popular OpenTelemetry span spec, but Vercel AI SDK doesn't conform to any of them so we still need to add some conversion logic within the client side. This PR does one additional thing for maintainability. Instead of directly insert the conversion logic within the exporter, this PR creates a plugin logic with which each integration library can register a "hook" for the attributes conversion. author: qidanrui
body:
feat: implement agent framework interoperability with custom tool system

## Description

This PR introduces a comprehensive custom tools system for MassGen, with a key focus on **agent framework interoperability**. The core innovation allows agents implemented in different frameworks (AG2, LangGraph, etc.) to be wrapped as tools and seamlessly used within MassGen, solving the long-standing challenge of cross-framework agent collaboration.

### Key Features

**🔧 Agent-as-Tool Interoperability**
- Wrap complex multi-agent systems from different frameworks as simple tool calls
- Enable agents built with AG2, LangGraph, or other frameworks to work together
- Demonstrated with two lesson planner examples:
  - `ag2_lesson_planner_tool`: AG2 nested chat architecture wrapped as a tool
  - `langgraph_lesson_planner_tool`: LangGraph state graph workflow wrapped as a tool

- Massgen agents use tools to call other frameworks’ agent. We pass original or processed messages from orchestrator to the tool through decorator @context_params. Users explicitly choose params to be injected from ExecutionContext
- “Prompt” is the processed messages from the orchestrator. We should never include agent system message in the prompt. Ideally we should need to change orchestrator/chat_agent behavior (orchestrator should not pass agent system message). Currently we work around it by removing agent system message from prompt.
- Backend can yield custom Tool result asynchronously now


### Technical Implementation

**New Components:**
- `massgen/tool/_extraframework_agents/`: Framework interoperability examples

## Type of change
- [x] New feature (`feat:`) - Non-breaking change which adds functionality

## Checklist
- [x] I have run pre-commit on my changed files and all checks pass
- [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

## Pre-commit status
```bash
# All pre-commit checks passing
```

## How to Test

### Prerequisites
```bash
# Install required dependencies for interoperability examples
pip install ag2 langgraph langchain-openai langchain-core

# Set OpenAI API key
export OPENAI_API_KEY=your_key_here
```

### Test CLI Command

**Test 1: AG2 + LangGraph Interoperability Demo**
```bash
massgen --config massgen/configs/tools/custom_tools/ag2_and_langgraph_lesson_planner.yaml \
  "Create a lesson plan for photosynthesis and compare the approaches"
```

**Test 2: Custom Tool with Claude**
```bash
massgen --config massgen/configs/tools/custom_tools/claude_custom_tool_example.yaml \
  "Use the custom tool to process data"
```

**Test 3: Run Unit Tests**
```bash
# Test AG2 lesson planner
pytest massgen/tests/test_ag2_lesson_planner.py -v

# Test LangGraph lesson planner
pytest massgen/tests/test_langgraph_lesson_planner.py -v
```

### Expected Results
- Two agents (ag2_planner and langgraph_planner) should both successfully create lesson plans
- Each agent uses a different framework (AG2 vs LangGraph) wrapped as a tool
- The output demonstrates cross-framework collaboration within MassGen
- Both lesson plans should be properly formatted and comprehensive

## Additional context

This PR addresses a fundamental challenge in the multi-agent ecosystem: **enabling collaboration between agents built with different frameworks**. By wrapping agents as tools, we create a universal interface that allows:

1. **Framework Agnostic Collaboration**: Agents don't need to know what framework their collaborators use
2. **Modular Agent Systems**: Complex multi-agent workflows can be composed from different framework components
3. **Ecosystem Integration**: Easy integration of existing agent systems built with AG2, LangGraph, CrewAI, etc.

The lesson planner examples showcase this capability concretely - AG2's nested chat and LangGraph's state graph can both be used as tools in the same MassGen workflow, demonstrating true framework interoperability.

---

### Known Limitations & Future Improvements

While this PR establishes the foundation for agent framework interoperability, several enhancements are planned for the next iteration:

#### 1. Parameter Standardization
**Current State:** Agent tools (ag2_lesson_planner, langgraph_lesson_planner) use `topic` as the input parameter.

**Improvement Needed:** Standardize to use `prompt` instead of `topic` for consistency with MassGen's general tool calling conventions.

```python
# Current
async def ag2_lesson_planner(topic: str, api_key: Optional[str] = None) -> ExecutionResult:

# Target
async def ag2_lesson_planner(prompt: str, api_key: Optional[str] = None) -> ExecutionResult:
```

This makes the tools more flexible for general-purpose use beyond lesson planning scenarios.

#### 2. Streaming Output Support
**Current State:** In `rich_terminal` display mode, agent tool results (from AG2 and LangGraph) are not streamed - they appear only after the entire execution completes.

**Improvement Needed:** Implement streaming output for agent tools to provide real-time visibility into:
- AG2's nested chat progression through multiple agents
- LangGraph's state transitions across workflow nodes
- Intermediate results from each sub-agent

**Technical Approach:** Leverage `ExecutionResult` with streaming generators or implement callback-based progress reporting.

#### 3. Enhanced Prompting Strategy for Agent Tools
**Context:** Drawing from the group chat adapter implementation experience, agent tools need sophisticated prompting when combined with MassGen's workflow toolkits (new_answer, vote).

**Improvement Needed:** Design and implement specialized prompts for agent tool invocation that:
- Guide agents on when to use workflow tools (new_answer, vote) vs. external framework tools
- Provide clear instructions on collaboration patterns
- Handle context passing between MassGen agents and wrapped framework agents

#### 4. Agent-as-Tool Orchestration Patterns

**Step 1: Parallel Execution with Voting**
```yaml
# Desired workflow:
# 1. Two agents run in parallel, each invoking their respective framework tools
# 2. Both generate streaming outputs visible to user
# 3. Results are collected and voting mechanism determines best answer
# 4. Final presentation is generated
```

**Step 2: Final Presentation Re-invocation**
```yaml
# Desired workflow:
# 1. Agents complete their individual tool-based work
# 2. During final presentation phase:
#    - Agent tool is re-invoked with refined context
#    - Generates a new, synthesized answer incorporating voting results
#    - Presents polished final output
```

#### 5. Add other framework agent tools
- OpenAIAssistant
- SmolAgent
- AgentScope
---

### Next Steps

These improvements are tracked for v0.1.4 and will build upon the interoperability foundation established in this PR. 

cc @Eric-Shang  for collaboration on prompting strategy based on group chat adapter learnings.

author: carlfriedrich
body:
This PR fixes the handling of `gitlab_runner_config_file` for container-based installs:

1. The `gitlab_runner_config_file` variable now intelligently defaults to the correct path for container-based installations. It automatically constructs the path using `gitlab_runner_container_mount_path` when `gitlab_runner_container_install` is true, removing the need for manual user configuration. This change makes the role more intuitive and prevents potential idempotency conflicts between system and container setup tasks.

2. The task for creating the system-level configuration directory with permissions `0700` was running unconditionally, even during container-based installations. This caused a file permission conflict with the container mount point setup, which already created this directory with `0755` permission, leading to two recurring changed states on every playbook run. Adding a conditional ensures this task is now skipped when `gitlab_runner_container_install` is true, resolving the idempotency issue.

This pull request introduces several major improvements to the backend, focusing on environment configuration, dependency injection, notification infrastructure, pipeline/reporting, and logging. The changes standardize and expand configuration management, add support for push notifications and real-time features, refactor dependency injection for better modularity, and introduce a new data pipeline/reporting service. Additionally, Python version requirements and dependencies are updated for broader compatibility and new features.

**Configuration and Environment Management:**

* Added a comprehensive `.env.example` with sections for Flask, database, Redis, and APNs configuration, making environment setup clearer and more robust.
* Moved configuration logic from `src/config.py` to a new `src/app_config.py`, improving structure and maintainability. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fabbf6cdd8169614341127f52b9f41f976cdf09d9657fddf300a1a37d0ae31fbR1-R52) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-24a3fe5c783755412cb9de83238b4dfd0699345bf50dcadc3ec23c6749361592L1-L35)
* Updated Python version requirement from 3.10 to 3.9 for broader compatibility (`.python-version`, `pyproject.toml`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-652bad7c1002badcf13f8de3a5096c2724ce54ae36cd68a21ad280547dff8e87L1-R1) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-50c86b7ed8ac2cf95bd48334961bf0530cdc77b5a56f852c5c61b89d735fd711L6-R36)

**Dependency Injection and Service Layer:**

* Refactored `DependencyContainer` to provide singletons for Redis and APNs services, and added new services for publishing and data pipelines, improving modularity and testability. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b30e487c880d0f20354acba5214f9beebf5b9b51fe54a4c025aff42d8c2b32d6R2-R12) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b30e487c880d0f20354acba5214f9beebf5b9b51fe54a4c025aff42d8c2b32d6R21-R46)
* Updated `create_app` to accept dependency injection modules/packages and wire them accordingly.

**Notification and Real-Time Infrastructure:**

* Added Redis and APNs service initialization in the DI container and app setup, enabling push notifications and pub/sub messaging. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b30e487c880d0f20354acba5214f9beebf5b9b51fe54a4c025aff42d8c2b32d6R2-R12) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6623d4a3b14abe033ee11425c6099609de50cf60d9f68fd33583e3d30c46030aL37-R52)
* Introduced Flask-SocketIO support for real-time features and updated app entrypoint to use `app.socketio.run`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-04791d82dd15fdd480f084d7ef65a10789fa5012cb7935f76080763444d48a00L20-R22) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6623d4a3b14abe033ee11425c6099609de50cf60d9f68fd33583e3d30c46030aL37-R52)
* Added ORM event handler to trigger notifications via Redis when product restock status changes.

**Pipeline and Reporting:**

* Added a new pipeline service and controller endpoint (`/pipelines`) for generating reports, with supporting configuration for preprocessing and paths. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-30e7fce3bc588cad86c7016625fe4022907c77fef6fe2c302c6b53862d1970a2L2-R9) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-30e7fce3bc588cad86c7016625fe4022907c77fef6fe2c302c6b53862d1970a2R18-R25) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-30f2c0c6c15210ad3d6c2ab80bab54c7c0ef7e68405dbb0b347c8dc453db086aR1-R7) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-3cbe7be5ab97148d84fb72c4a8299ab40cfb34b8d128e97ac5674d19dc1777ceR1-R74) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-b30e487c880d0f20354acba5214f9beebf5b9b51fe54a4c025aff42d8c2b32d6R21-R46) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-463bc0b4b46192dc10d87901b462b6cf3ad02f6bd28a2dbe31fab9370fa288daR1-R3)

body:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

- Simplify config deployment using file-based approach instead of git cloning

- Alt+Ctrl+H/L: Move workspace between monitors
- Workspace P: Dedicated floating workspace for btop monitoring
- Mouse follows focus across monitors

- Alt+H/J/K/L: Navigate between windows (vi-style)

- Alt+1-9, Alt+P: Switch workspaces
- Alt+R: Enter resize mode

- Zero gaps between windows for maximum screen real estate
